body: PRESS STATEMENT November 20, 2024 Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago welcomes back graduates of the NBI Academy during the 2024 “Balik Akademya” organized by the NBI Investigators Mutual Benefit Association, Inc. (NBI-IMBAI). The Balik Akademya is celebrated yearly to foster camaraderie and rekindle friendship among all NBI Agents, including retired NBI Agents. Among the notable retired agents include retired Regional Director Crisostomo F. Balancio (Batch 12-Class 1966), former Deputy Director Filomeno S. Bautista (Batch 15-Class 1968) and Ex Judge Domingo Maristela (Batch 19-Class 1972). In his inspirational message, Santiago mentioned to be proactive in investigation and never put the organization in bad light. “Tumaas na ang kredibilidad at tiwala ng taong bayan sa NBI, ituloy tuloy lang natin ang magandang serbisyo para sa bayan,” Santiago said. Meanwhile, as part of the anniversary celebration, the IMBAI came up with the NBI Director’s Cup 2024 (Level II shooting competition) on November 16&17, 2024 at the Iron Sight Shooting Range in Silang, Cavite. The shooting competition has a widest participation from agents and operatives from Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao with a total of 421 shooters. The 2-day event concluded very well with no untoward incident noted. Magmula ngayon weekly na ang shooting natin at libre ang bala, Santiago said during the Monday Directorial Staff Meeting.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 28, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES SECOND MINOR VICTIM OF ONLINE SEXUAL EXPLOITATION IN BATANGAS FOLLOW-UP OPERATION PASAY CITY, Philippines – On March 25, 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation – Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-VAWCD) successfully rescued another minor victim of Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) in a follow-up operation in Tanauan, Batangas. The rescue was initiated following a previous successful NBI-VAWCD operation that resulted in the arrest of a facilitator and the rescue of an initial victim. Information provided by the first survivor led the NBI-VAWCD to the identity of the second minor being exploited by the same facilitator. In a coordinated effort with the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD) of Tanauan, the Philippine National Police (PNP), and the Department of Education (DepEd), NBI agents conducted the rescue at a local public high school. With the assistance of the victim’s class adviser, the minor was identified and safely taken into protective custody. She has since been turned over to the CSWD for trauma-informed intervention and support. Evidence gathered from the minor-victims has led to additional charges against the Subject for violations of Republic Act No. 11930, also known as the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act, and Republic Act No. 9208, the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by R.A. 10364 and R.A. 11862. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag praised the NBI-VAWCD for their relentless efforts that culminated in the successful rescue of the minor victim from trafficking. He highlighted that this operation signifies the Bureau’s commitment to pursuing every lead, emphasizing that the NBI will not stop at the initial arrest but will continue its operations until every victim is rescued and brought to safety. Director Matibag assured the public that the NBI will continue to work tirelessly to prevent further victimization and bring perpetrators to justice, calling for community support and vigilance in the collective fight against human trafficking. #NBIServes
title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI-CCD Nabs Individual in Pasay City for Cyber-Related Estafa and Multi-Million Peso Investment Scheme PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) has successfully arrested an individual involved in an investment scam targeting aspiring Overseas Filipino Workers (OFWs). The operation took place on February 10, 2026 that led to the arrest of the Subject during an entrapment at a local mall. The investigation began following a complaint from a victim who was lured into a fraudulent foreign exchange trading scheme. The Subject allegedly utilized the messaging app Telegram to manage an investment group, enticing members with the promise of “faster income” and guaranteed returns on investment (ROI). Driven by the prospect of financial security before working abroad, the Complainant transferred a total of Php 957,700.00 across several transactions. This included a final “third ride” payment of Php 60,000.00, which the Subject claimed would double in value. When the promised returns failed to materialize despite repeated demands, the Subject attempted to solicit an additional Php 4,000,000.00 from the victim. Realizing the fraudulent nature of the business, the Complainant coordinated with the NBI-CCD. An entrapment operation was conducted at a restaurant inside a Pasay City mall, where a meeting had been scheduled for the delivery of the additional investment. The Subject was subsequently arrested by NBI-CCD operatives while in the process of accepting the marked currency.” The Subject was presented for inquest proceedings and now faces formal charges for Estafa under Article 315, paragraph 2(a) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno lauded the swift action of the Cybercrime Division and issued a sharp rebuke to those preying on the hard-earned savings of Filipinos. “This is a stern warning to criminals: stop your illegal activities or face justice behind bars,” said Acting Director Magno. “The NBI remains dedicated to upholding justice and protecting our citizens from digital predators.” The NBI advises the public to be cautious of investment opportunities shared through private messaging apps that promise “guaranteed” or “unusually high” returns. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]
title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 27, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two individuals in Paranaque City for trafficking of minors and rescued eleven (11) victims. Two Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted by HTRAD Agents together with representatives from a non-governmental organization on March 22, 2025. Poseur-customer met with the Subjects in a fast food chain in Sucat, Paranaque, where the Subjects presented the minor victims to the poseur-customer, who in turn was to choose among the victims. The subject told the poseur-customer that the fee for sexual service of the chosen victim is Php 2,500.00. After receiving the Php 2,500.00 boodle money, the Subject and his cohort were placed under arrest. A total of eleven (11) minor victims, with ages 14 to 16 years old, were taken to HTRAD office for their sworn statements under the supervision of DSWD Social Workers. They will undergo rehabilitative and protective programs and will be provided counselling and temporary shelter. Subjects were brought to NBI-HTRAD office for the standard operating procedures. They were presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice, Task Force Against Trafficking for violation of R.A. No. 9208 otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, R.A. No. 7610 or the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act and R.A. No. 11930 or the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM) Act.
title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the filing of several criminal charges by the NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) against eleven (11) individuals who were involved in the untimely death of Christine Angelica F. Dacera. Included in the charge is a Police Official who first conducted the autopsy on the cadaver of Victim Dacera. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the charged individuals as MARK ANTHONY ROSALES, ROMEL GALIDO Y DALURO, JOHN PASCUAL DELA SERNA III Y REYES, DARWIN JOSEPH MACALLA Y DE LEON, GREGORIO ANGELO RAFAEL DE GUZMAN Y DELA FUENTE, JEZREEL RAPINAN Y PAMISA, ALAIN CHEN Y DAYANAN, REYMAR ENGLIS Y MABINI, ATTY. NEPTALI G. MAROTO, LOUIE DELIMA Y SUNGA, and P/MAJ MICHAEL NICK W. SARMIENTO, M.D. OIC-Director Distor said that upon directive of Department of Justice (DOJ) Secretary Menardo Guevarra and the letter of Sharon Rose Dacera (victim’s mother) requesting a parallel investigation on her daughter’s death, NBI conducted an investigation on the death of Dacera. Testimonies of the witnesses and persons involved revealed that on December 27, 2020, Dacera together with her friends Subjects GALIDO, ENGLIS, DELIMA, DELA SERNA, and RAPINAN booked an overnight stay in City Garden Hotel in Makati City starting from December 31, 2020 to January 1, 2021. According to the Duty Manager of the hotel he was a friend of Dacera’s companion and asked by Dacera’s group to facilitate their booking and accommodated the booking. Dacera’s group was first designated to Room 2309 but later transferred to Room 2209 due to the Air-Conditioning malfunction. In the evening of December 31, 2020, Victim Dacera together with her friends partied in their hotel room while drinking several liquors. Coincidentally, while waiting for the New Year countdown, ED (one of the companions of Victim Dacera in Room 2209) brought them to Room 2207 where his friend identified as DHEEJ is also checked-in. CCTV footages revealed that the victim and her friends were seen go back and forth in Rooms 2207 and 2209. Re-autopsy on the cadaver of Victim Dacera revealed that the cause of her death was microscopic evidence of peri-aortic hemorrhages and aortic wall disruption, suspicious for a bleeding dissecting aneurysm based on the review of slides of PNP Crime Laboratory. Toxicology examinations on the cadaver of the victim showed the presence of DILTIAZEM, a prescription drug for the management of hypertension. Results of the NBI Investigation revealed the glaring inconsistencies in the PNP autopsy report. Results of the autopsy report conducted by the NBI- Medico Legal Division Chief revealed that in contrast to the autopsy report of P/Maj. Sarmiento, M.D., Victim’s urinary bladder was full of urine and in fact the NBI Forensic Team was able to extract 130 ml of urine and no abrasion was found in her labia majora. PNP Crime Laboratory turned-over to the NBI the laboratory result of two pieces of cotton found inside Room 2209. According to the report the two pieces of cotton showed the presence of Flouromethamphetamine and Methamphetamine. According to the testimonies of the witnesses who checked-in at Room 2207, around 03:00 a.m. in the morning, Victim Dacera told them that she did not want to be at Room 2209 because her companions because they were high for taking party drugs in contrast to the sworn statements of the victim’s friends and companions at Room 2209. Thus, based on the forensic evidences and testimonies of the witnesses, NBI-DID filed before the Department of Justice (DOJ): Violation of Sec. 3 (a) and penalized under Sec. 5 of the R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002) against Subject ROSALES for introducing the party drugs to his companions; Violation of Section 3 (k) and penalized under Sec. 26 of R.A. 9165 against Subjects ROSALES and GALIDO for delivering and giving away the party drugs; Perjury against Subjects GALIDO, DELA SERNA, and MACALLA for providing false testimonies; Obstruction of Justice against Subjects ROSALES, GALIDO, DELA SERNA, DE GUZMAN, RAPINAN, CHEN, ENGLIS, MACALLA, and ATTY. MAROTO for giving false or fabricated information to mislead or prevent the law enforcement agencies form apprehending the offenders; Reckless Imprudence Resulting in Homicide against Subjects DELA SERNA, RAPINAN, CHEN, and DELIMA for recklessly neglect the condition of Victim Dacera which led on to her untimely death; Article 171 par. 4 of the RPC (Falsification of Official Document by Public Officer) against POLICE MAJOR SARMIENTO, M.D. for declaring untruthful findings on his autopsy report.
title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

body: A seven year old boy who was abducted was rescued and his kidnappers arrested during an operation by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents in a Manila mall recently. Subjects are identified as: RONEL SANTIAGO aka “BRYAN ANTOS”, a resident of Malabon City ; and RONA SABROSO GADOR, with address at San Jose Del Monte and Malolos, Bulacan. Investigation report of the NBI – National Capital Region office disclosed that on December 14, 2012, it received a complaint from the mother of the kidnapped victim informing that the day before, December 13, her son JC was kidnapped from the residence in Marilao, Bulacan. The kidnapper is allegedly a friend of the victim’s father who introduced himself as a certain Kuya Jason. He demanded P20,000.00 for the release of her son and a threat of possible harm or death. The victim’s mother relayed to the NBI of several exchange of cellphone messages between the mother and the subject. It was demanded that the ransom money be through money transfer via Cebuana Lhuillier. Subsequently, a rescue operation was planned, in which the money through wire transfer will be sent to the kidnapper with a tracking or claim number. Numerous informants were tasked to monitor several branches of Cebuana Lhuillier within Metro Manila to identify the person who would claim the wired transfer amount. The suspect also instructed that the amount be in the name of a certain Brian Santos as claimant. On the night of December 14, 2012, an informant called the NBI and said that he saw a boy resembling the kidnap-victim based on the photos given to informants. The boy was in the company of a man and a woman who entered the Cebuana Lluillier branch inside the Odeon Mall located at the corner of C.M. Recto and Rizal Avenue Sta. Cruz Manila. NBI operatives rushed to the place and they saw the duo in the company of a boy waiting for their turn to be serviced. Certain of the identity of the kidnap-victim, the operatives waited for Subjects to finish their transaction. After they received the money- transfer demanded, the pair hurriedly left the counter. At this point, NBI operatives approached, introduced themselves and arrested the subjects while the boy was rescued. Found in the possession of the subjects are: a postal ID in the name of Brian Santos, an electronically validated PERA PADALA claim receipt and Santos’s cellphone containing series of messages sent to and from the complainant. When asked of their true identities, they themselves as RONEL SANTIAGO and as RONA GADOR. The next day, the subjects were brought to the Manila Prosecutor’s Office and recommended for prosecution for Violation of Article 267 otherwise known as Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation today said operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) have arrested an individual representing herself as sister of the late Senator Miriam Defensor Santiago, for alleged Estafa and Usurpation of Authority on May 29, 2017. NBI-AOTCD received a complaint concerning a certain ATTY. PAULA DIMPNA BEATRIZ PALMA DEFENSOR for alleged Estafa and Usurpation of Authority. Complainant met the subject at the Department of Justice (DOJ) sometime in July 2016 when she was following-up a case against her. Subject, who represented herself as the sister of the late Senator Miriam Defensor Santiago, a lawyer and a consultant of DOJ Secretary Vitaliano Aguirre, offered the Complainant her services to be her lawyer for the pending cases. Induced by Subject’s representation, Complainant hired Subject as her lawyer. Subject even appeared as Complainant’s counsel in her pending cases before RTC Branch 76, San Mateo, Rizal and at RTC Branch 87, Quezon City. Consequently, on several occasions, Subject demanded and received from Complainant acceptance and other fees for her services, totaling Php 580,000.00. Complainant however learned later on from DOJ USEC Raymund Mecate that there is no consultant at the DOJ. Moreover, Complainant also found out from a long time staff of the late Senator that the real ATTY. PAULA DIMPNA BEATRIZ PALMA DEFENSOR is living abroad. It was then that the Complainant sought the assistance of the NBI. Further investigation conducted revealed that the Subject is using several names and aliases. It was also discovered Subject’s real name is MYRNA ROSALES VELEZ who has numerous cases such as Swindling and Illegal Recruitment under various names and aliases. Verification conducted with RTC Branch 20, Malolos, Bulacan revelead that Subject has an outstanding Warrant of Arrest for Estafa issued on May 24, 2007. The NBI-AOTCD also confirmed that the Warrant of Arrest issued against the Subject for Illegal Recruitment issued on December 8, 2008 is also outstanding. On May 29, 2017, NBI-AOTCD operatives arrested Subject MYRNA ROSALES VELEZ after they were informed that the Subject was at the premises of NBI Clearance Building. The outstanding Warrant of Arrest against the Subject was likewise served upon her. Subject is currently detained at the NBI Detention Facility. NBI-AOTCD is still the process of verifying other Warrants of arrest issued by various courts.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 04, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) arrested WYETH NAVALLES y LARA and LEILA NAVALLES y LARA in Guagua, Pampanga for Robbery with Violence Against or Intimidation of Persons by way of Extortion under the Revised Penal Code (RPC), as amended. The operation stemmed from a complaint filed against Subject Wyeth for alleged extortion. The Complainant reported that he had hired Subject Wyeth, a licensed Customs Broker, to handle his importation process in the Philippines. They agreed on an all-inclusive fee of Php 500,000.00. Despite proper settlement of Php220,938.00 in customs duties and taxes, Subject Wyeth claimed that the shipment was held due to a misdeclaration. Furthermore, Subject Wyeth demanded an additional Php 1,900,000.00 in “grease money,” which was to be distributed among various Bureau of Customs (BOC) divisions, as well as the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) and the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), to facilitate the release of the Complainant’s importation. Thus, prompting the Complainant to file a complaint. After coordinating with the BOC, a joint entrapment operation was planned to apprehend the subject. On June 3, 2025, the Complainant, together with the joint elements of NBI-OTCD and BOC-CIIS, MICP, proceeded to a coffee shop in Ermita, Manila, where the demanded money would be given to Subject Wyeth. The joint operatives strategically positioned themselves discreetly in the vicinity and positively identified Subject Wyeth along with a companion, later identified as her sister, Subject Leila. Upon handing over the marked money, Subject Wyeth executed an Acknowledgement Receipt and gave it to the Complainant. At this juncture, the joint operatives immediately approached the subjects and announced their arrest. The arrested individuals were taken to the NBI-OTCD office for post-arrest procedures. Subject Wyeth underwent an Ultraviolet Light Examination at the Forensic Chemistry Division (FCD), which yielded positive results for fluorescent powder dust, indicating physical contact with the entrapment money. Thereafter, the arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor in Manila for the aforementioned violation. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-OTCD for the successful operation and emphasized the importance of smooth inter-agency coordination in conducting law enforcement operations.
title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 30, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the operations against syndicated pilferages and theft of imported Customs containers, the NBI-Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) arrested JOHN M. AVELES MENDOZA and ANGELO RAMOS in a hot pursuit operation on July 12, 2025, at the Arctic Cold Storage in Cainta, Rizal, for Qualified Theft and violation of Republic Act No. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed against JOHN A. MENDOZA and ANGELO RAMOS, driver and helper, respectively, of JBIZ Cargo Services, who hauled the Customs’ sealed and GPS tracker-equipped container for delivery to the said cold storage facility. Investigation by the NBI-OLDO agents revealed that en route to Cainta, Rizal, Subjects tampered the Customs seal and GPS tracker, opened the container, pilfered its contents, and thereafter carried on their trip. An anomaly indicative of a breach on the GPS registered in the monitor of the Bureau of Customs, which alerted the broker, who immediately filed a Complaint with the NBI-OLDO. Agents of the NBI-OLDO, along with the BOC Examiners, proceeded to the Arctic Cold Storage and in the presence of the Department of Agriculture-BAI Personnel, the owner of the truck and herein Subjects, opened the above container. A spot inventory was conducted, showing that 224 boxes of imported meat products were missing, with the approximate amount of P1,614,000.00. Subjects Mendoza and Ramos were placed under arrest and were presented for Inquest Proceeding before the DOJ in Manila for the aforementioned violations. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-OLDO for the successful operation, which resulted in the arrest of Subjects. He said that this operation strengthens the NBI’s commitment against Syndicated pilferages and theft of imported Customs containers.

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT S E C A D V IS O R Y The Commission has received information that MONEY GAME HUB / MGH TRADING OPC (“MGH”) is engaged in UNAUTHORIZED investment-taking activities. MONEY GAME HUB / MGH TRADING OPC is allegedly a perfume-distribution marketing company and is headed by ALEXANDER LIBRES SALVADOR who entices the public to join the company and invest a minimum of Five Hundred Pesos (Php500.00) and promises seven times (7X) return on investment for a period of 40 days. Hence, an initial investment of Php500.00 will have a return of Php3,500.00 after 40 days as shown in the table below: The Money Game Hub is designed as a Multi-level marketing platform providing:  PASSIVE INCOME PLAYER PACKAGES - CHALK PLAYER PACKAGE-Php500.00; - DIME PLAYER PACKAGE-Php1,000.00; - SHARP PLAYER PACKAGE-Php5,000.00; - SHARK PLAYER PACKAGE-Php20,000.00; and - WHALE PLAYER PACKAGE-Php50,000.00.  DIRECT REFERRAL BONUS - CHALK PLAYER-20% - DIME PLAYER-25% - SHARP PLAYER-30% - SHARK PLAYER-35%; and - WHALE PLAYER-50%  INDIRECT REFERRAL BONUS of 1% to every up-line member, chained all the way up to infinity (CEO of company).  ENCASHMENT BONUS-1% of cash taken from every cash withdrawal and given to the next up-line member.  MONEY SPIN (A casino feature / game of chance) For joining members: P5000=1 ticket, P20000=3 tickets, P50000=5 tickets. Also cash payments: P500=5 ticket spins, P1000=10 ticket spins, P5000=50 ticket spins, and P10000=100 ticket spins. As the aforementioned schemes involve the sale of securities to the public, the Securities Regulation Code (SRC) requires that these securities are duly registered and that the concerned corporation and/or its agents have appropriate registration and/or license to sell such securities to the public pursuant to Section 8 and 28 of the SRC. The public is hereby informed that MONEY GAME HUB is not registered as a corporation and partnership. However, MGH TRADING OPC is registered with the Commission as a One Person Corporation. Nonetheless, both MONEY GAME HUB / MGH TRADING OPC are not authorized to solicit investments from the public as they did not secure prior registration and/or license to solicit investments from the Commission as prescribed under Section 8 of the Securities and Exchange Commission. The public is reminded that the issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation only grants the said entity juridical personality but does not constitute an authority or license for the corporation to engage in activities such as solicitation of investments, issuance of investments contracts, offering and sale of investment contracts that require a secondary license. Consequently, those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents of MONEY GAME HUB / MGH TRADING OPC in selling or convincing people to invest in their investment schemes including solicitations or recruitment through the internet may likewise be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the SRC and penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million Pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or maximum penalty of Twenty-One (21) years imprisonment or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC. Also, those who invite or recruit others to join or invest in such venture or offer investment contracts or securities to the public may incur criminal liability, or otherwise be sanctioned or penalized accordingly as held by the Supreme Court in the case of Securities and Exchange Commission vs. Oudine Santos (G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). In view thereof, the public is hereby advised to STOP INVESTING in the investment schemes being offered by any individual or group or persons allegedly acting for or on behalf of MONEY GAME HUB / MGH TRADING OPC. Furthermore, the names of all those involved will be reported to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) so that the appropriate penalties and/or taxes be correspondingly assessed. Should you have any information regarding the operation of the subject entity, please call the Enforcement and Investor Protection Department at telephone numbers (02) 8818-6047 or send your report to the EIPD at epd@sec.gov.ph. For guidance of the public. Pasay City, 23 August 2021.

SECADVISORY 27 June 2013 Mandaluyong Philippines EMAIL SCAM: "CHANGE OF SUPPLIERBANK DETAILS" The public is warned to take precautionary care and diligence In transactingthru email with foreign suppliers/manufacturers. Before transacting, carefully verify first whether the email address of the email message you have received and replying to is the correct email address of the supplier and manufacturer you are dealing with. It has been reported to authorities that there is an email scam described as "Change of Supplier Bank Details" whereby the scammer, pretending to be the supplier/manufacturer sends fictitious emails (very similar to suppliers' real email.Ex.:miller@1yahoo.comchangedtomiler@yahoo.com.) to the prospective victim, advising the latter that his bank account has been changed. Thus, the victim is misled into remitting his payment to the wrong bank account, consequently to the wrong payee.
title: Email Scam : Change of Supplier Bank Details

body: SEC ADVISORY The Commission has received information that individuals or groups of persons representing BROILERPRENUER CORPORATION doing business under the name BroilerPRENEUR are enticing the public to invest in the said entity online and through their website https://www.broilerpreneur.com/. Per records of the Securities and Exchange Commission, BROILERPRENUER CORPORATION is registered in the Commission’s database as a stock corporation with company registration no. CS201908435. It was issued its certificate of incorporation on 27 May 2019. Its primary purpose To engage in, conduct and carry on the business of consumer services, production, buying, selling, distributing, direct selling, and online marketing at wholesale and retail of chix, chicken and other related products. However, BROILERPRENUER CORPORATION is not authorized to solicit investments from the public as the above-mentioned corporation did not secure prior registration and/or license to solicit investment from the commission as prescribed under Section 8 of the Securities Regulation Code. Accordingly, BROILERPRENUER CORPORATION is engaged in the poultry business employing the “farm to fork concept of broiler” and promises to the public 100% guaranteed return of investment. The business concept runs for 60 days and divided as follows:  3 Days for the buying of chicks;  45 Days breeding; and  12 Days dressing plant and selling. = Total of 60 days. The said investment scheme is illustrated below: CAPITAL AFTER 2 MOS. AFTER 4 MOS. AFTER 6 MOS. AFTER 12 MOS. 1,000 2,000 4,000 6,000 12,000 5,000 10,000 20,000 30,000 60,000 50,000 100,000 200,000 300,000 600,000 500,000 1,000,000 2,000,000 3,000,000 6,000,000 1,000,000 2,000,000 4,000,000 6,000,000 12,000,000 5,000,000 10,000,000 20,000,000 30,000,000 60,000,000 Where the scheme involves the sale of securities to the public, the Securities Regulation Code (SRC) requires that the issuing person and/or entity must be a registered corporation with SEC, the said securities offered are duly registered and that the appropriate license and/or permit to sell securities to the public are issued to the corporation and/or its agents, pursuant to the provisions of section 8 and 28 of the SRC. The public is hereby advised to exercise caution in investing their money in these types of schemes which may turn out to be Fraudulent Investment Schemes, involving the sale of unregistered securities. Those who act as salesman, broker or agents of BROILERPRENUER CORPORATION in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered, including solicitations or recruitment may likewise be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the SRC and penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million Pesos (P5,000,000) or imprisonment of Twenty One (21) years or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC. Likewise, those who sell or offer securities the public, may be held criminally liable or accordingly sanctioned or penalized pursuant to the Supreme Court Decision in the case of Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Vs. Oudine Santos (G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). Should you have any information regarding the operations of the subject corporation, please call the Enforcement and Investor Protection Department at telephone numbers (02)818-6337 and (02)818- 5324. For the guidance of the public.

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This is to inform the public that TETHER-PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM /TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED IS NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENTS FROM THE PUBLIC. This Advisory is prompted by the information received and gathered by the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) that individuals or group of persons headed by its CEO, RENDON DURAN is soliciting investments from the public purportedly to be invested in foreign exchange and cryptocurrency trading. TETHER-PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM/TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED entices the public to invest online or through the internet an amount ranging from 10 USDT up to 300,000 USDT (equivalent to P557.50 up to P1,672,500) where investors can earn guaranteed 3% to 10% daily profit in 70 days or equivalent to 210% for the same period (Php 1,169 up to Php 3,515,250). The said entity likewise offers: 1) ROI Percent Upgrades and 2) Commission Levels. TETHER-PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM/TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED appears to be engaged in a fraudulent scheme of offering and selling unregistered securities in the form of investment contracts in violation of Sections 8 and 26 of the Securities Regulation Code. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers, agents, representatives, promoters, recruiters, uplines, influencers, endorsers, abetters and enablers of TETHER- PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM/TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED vis-à-vis RENDON DURAN in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered by said entity including solicitations and recruitment through the internet may be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the SRC and penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or penalty of Twenty-one (21) years of imprisonment or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC (G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). In view thereof, the public is advised NOT TO INVEST or STOP INVESTING in any investment scheme being offered by TETHER-PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM /TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED vis-à-vis RENDON DURAN as well as to any other entities having the same or similar schemes and to exercise caution in dealing with any individuals or group of persons soliciting investments or recruiting investors for and on behalf of TETHER-PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM /TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED vis-à-vis RENDON DURAN. Should you have any information regarding any investment solicitation by any individuals or group of individuals on behalf of TETHER-PAY/TETHER.PAY.COM /TETHER PAY LTD./TETHER PAY LIMITED vis-à-vis RENDON DURAN please send your report to the ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT at epd@sec.gov.ph. For the guidance of the public. Pasay City, 27 December 2022.

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY The Securities and Exchange Commission has received information that individuals or group of persons representing IX TRADE/IXTRADE with website, http://www.ixtrade.net and through FACEBOOK pages, “IXTRADE Legitimate”, “Ixtrade.net”, “IXTRADE -TEAM PANALO” and “INGRID ARCHE” are engaged in UNAUTHORIZED investment-taking activities. IX TRADE/IXTRADE guarantees that for money invested ranging from Php500- Php20,000, investors shall earn 150% after 12 days with a referral bonus of 20%. Page 1 of 2 Allegedly, the earnings shall be generated from trading in the forex and cryptocurrency markets. As the aforementioned scheme involves the offering and sale of securities to the public, the Securities Regulation Code (SRC) requires that these securities are duly registered with the Commission and that the concerned corporation and/or its agents have appropriate registration and/or license to sell such securities to the public pursuant to Section 8 and 28 of the SRC. The public is hereby informed that IX TRADE /IXTRADE is NOT registered with the Commission either as a corporation or a partnership. It is not authorized to solicit investments from the public as it did not secure prior registration and/or license to solicit investments from the Commission as prescribed under Section 8 and 28 of the SRC. Further, IX TRADE/IXTRADE is also NOT REGISTERED either as a crowdfunding intermediary or a funding portal under SEC Memorandum Circular No. 14, Series of 2019 or the Rules and Regulations Governing Crowdfunding. Accordingly, those who invite or recruit other people to join or invest in this venture or offer investment contracts or securities to the public may be held criminally liable or accordingly sanctioned or penalized in accordance with the Supreme Court decision in the case of SEC vs. Oudine Santos (G.R. No. 195542, March 19, 2014). The Commission further reminds the public, that as early as 31 October 2018 the Commission issued an advisory for the public to stop engaging in Foreign Exchange Trading and to stop investing in investment platforms of commodity futures, contracts for difference, indices, binary options and the like. In view thereof, the public is hereby advised to exercise caution before investing in these kinds of activities and to take the necessary precautions in dealing with IX TRADE/ IXTRADE and its representatives. The Commission urges anyone who has knowledge or information about any business transactions involving these securities or investment opportunities to report such activities so that appropriate actions could be taken through the email of the Enforcement and Investor Protection Department at epd@sec.gov.ph. For the guidance of the public. Pasay City, 15 April 2021 Page 2 of 2

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT MAG-INGAT SA SCAM! Patuloy na kumakalat ang scams na nambibiktima sa publiko na sumali sa anumang negosyo o pagkakakitaan na may pangakong tubo na saklaw ng produktong pinansyal na tinatawag na investment/securities. Para ‘wag maloko ng INVESTMENT SCAM, tandaan ang mga sumusunod: A. MAG-RESEARCH, MAGING MAPANURI AT MAGTANONG. 1. KILALANIN ANG KAUSAP O ANG NAG-AALOK. a. Alamin ang kanyang pangalan, saan siya nagtratrabaho at kung ano kanyang posisyon. Kuhanin ang mga importanteng detalye tulad ng company I.D., government I.D., contact number at e-mail address. b. Kung ang iyong kausap ay ‘di mo kilala, isang kamag-anak o kaibigan, siya ba ay isang ahenteng lisensyado ng SEC upang mangalap ng investment o manghikayat ng pamumuhunan sa pamamagitan ng securities? I-verify sa: http://cmprs.sec.gov.ph/ ‘Wag basta magtiwala kahit sa taong kilala mo. 2. ALAMIN ANG KUMPANYA. a. Ang kumpanya ba na nag-aalok ng investment ay lisensiyado ng SEC? Tandaan, ‘di sapat ang rehistrayon sa SEC bilang isang korporasyon o sa ibang ahensiya ng pamahalaan gaya ng Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Cooperative Development Authority at Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) para masabing ito ay legal at may kaukulang lisensyang mag- alok ng “investment opportunities/securities.” Ang pag-aalok ng pamumuhunan o investment ay isang gawaing pinangangasiwaan ng gobyerno kaya dapat may permit o lisensya sa SEC (maaaring Permit to Offer and Sell Securities o Securities Broker) ang korporasyon. Ang negosyong maaring pasukin ng isang kumpanya ay dapat alinsunod sa rehistrasyong ipinagkaloob ng SEC na makikita sa primary purpose sa Articles of Incorporation, lalo na kung ito ay tungkol sa pangangalakal ng pera, pagpapautang, pagbebenta ng mga instrumento ng pananalapi o kapital at iba pang uri ng negosyo. b. Ito ba ay may inaalok na produktong pang-konsyumer? Ang produkto ba ay naka-rehistro sa kaukulang ahensya ng pamahalaan? Bilang halimbawa: PRODUKTO AHENSYA WEBSITE Food, food www.fda.gov.ph supplements, drugs, Food and Drugs cosmetics Authority househould hazardous, pesticides, medical devices, diagnostics and veterinary products. Livestocks, poultry Bureau of https://www.bai.gov.ph/ and allied industries Animals Industry Condominium Department of https://dhsud.gov.ph/ projects and Housing Human and Urban Settlements and Development Urban Development (DHSUD) Crypto or Virtual BSP http://www.bsp.gov.ph/ Currencies Virtual Currency (VC) Exchanges c. Ito ba ay may “direct selling” o “multi-level marketing scheme”? Alamin kung ang scheme ay isang “pyramiding” sa pamamagitan ng mga sumusunod: Filename Link a. Anti-Pyramiding Videos https://www.dsap.ph/anti-pyramiding- video/ b. 8-point test https://www.dsap.ph/wp- content/uploads/2018/08/8-Point-Test- POSTER-HIRES-FILE-WFDSA-edited.jpg Page 2 d. Ito ba ay may opisina na maaring bisitahin? Alamin kung ito talaga ang kanilang opisina sa pamamagitan ng pagtatanong sa barangay, building administrator o sa Business Permits and Licensing Office ng Lungsod/Munisipyo kung saan matatagpuan ang nasabing kumpanya. Kung wala, mag-ingat sa mga ganitong kumpanya. e. Ito ba ay may kaso o reklamo sa SEC? Nakasama ba ito sa Advisory o Cease and Desist Order (CDO) na inisyu ng SEC? Bisitahin ang aming website sa www.sec.gov.ph o opisyal na Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/PhilippineSEC/ o sa pamamagitan ng pag-click sa link: Link Listahan ng “Advisory” https://www.sec.gov.ph/investors- education-and- information/advisories/ Listahan ng “Cease and Desist https://www.sec.gov.ph/sec- Order” issuances/cease-and-desist-orders/ Listahan ng kompanyang may https://www.sec.gov.ph/sec- “Revocation Order” issuances/other-orders/order-of- revocation/ 3. MAGTANONG AT KUMONSULTA Kumonsulta sa mga propesyunal, lehitimo o kilalang stock broker/dealer/agents (mga ahente na lisensyadong bumili or magbenta ng mga produktong pinansyal gaya ng securities) at sa mga tamang ahensiya ng pamahalaan bago magdesisyong mamuhunan. 4. HUMINGI NG KOPYA NG MGA DOKUMENTO. a. Bago sumali sa isang negosyo, humingi ng mga “Certificate of Incorporation,” “Articles of Incorporation,” “prospectus,” katalogo, legal na dokumento at kasulatan tungkol sa pinansyal na kalagayan ng kompanya. Bago pirmahan ang anumang kasulatan, kailangang may kasunduan na maari ninyong bawiin ang inyong pera na naaayon sa inyong kagustuhan. Page 3 b. May pinapakita ba silang Audited Financial Statements na pina- receive sa BIR o sa SEC? c. Humingi ng opisyal na resibo (Official Receipt) mula sa kumpanya at tao na inyong naka-transaksyon sa negosyo. Mahalaga ang mga impormasyon upang ang mga “investor” ay magkaroon ng “informed decision” kung saan at paano ginagamit ang perang ipinagkatiwala at ang mga panganib o “investment risks” na kaakibat ng negosyo. B. MGA RED FLAGS o SENYALES NG ISANG SCAM 1. Ang nanghihikayat pumasok sa investment ay walang permit sa SEC (iba pa ang rehistrasyon bilang korporasyon) at ang mga produkto ay walang kaukulang lisensya galing sa tamang ahensya ng gobyerno. 2. “Sounds too good to be true” o ang interest o tubong pinapangako ay napakalaki o ang kita ay umaasa sa “invite” o “recruitment” ng ibang tao. 3. May mga mali (typos o grammar) sa kanilang “advertisements” o “posts.” 4. Nanghihikayat at nakikipag-usap lamang gamit ang social media o messaging app at hindi personal na sinasabi kung saan matatagpuan ang kanilang opisina o ito ay hindi makita sa kanilang “website” o “social media account.” 5. Paggamit ng pekeng “social media accounts” at “websites.” Kung magiging mapanuri, makikita na hindi totoo ang kanilang pangalan, phone numbers, credentials, testimonials, larawan at gumagamit ng piktyur ng mga sikat o prominenteng tao upang makapanghikayat. 6. Nang-eenganyong sumali sa nasabing investment sa pamamagitan ng “PM me for details” o “PM is the key.” Tinatago nila ang kanilang totoong aktibidad o kung paano nila pinapatakbo ang kanilang operasyon. 7. Hindi nagbibigay ng kopya ng kontrata, prospectus, katalogo, legal na dokumento at kasulutan. 8. Hindi mo maintindihan kung paano ka kikita. Gumagamit ng mga “technical explanations” at nakalilitong paliwanag. ‘Wag mag-invest sa mga bagay na di mo maiintindihan. Page 4 9. Kapag bayaran na ang usapan, ipinadedeposito ang pera sa isang “account” na nakapangalan sa isang indibidwal at hindi sa korporasyon. 10. Nagpo-post ng piktyur ng malaking halaga ng salapi, tseke o resibo na kumakatawan sa kinita diumano o larawan ng mga mamahaling kotse o kagamitang nakamit upang masabi na sila ay kumikita ng malaki sa nasabing programa. 11. Nangangako ng “guaranteed investment returns” o “high investment returns” sa mga “trivial tasks” tulad ng “click and earn,” “watch and earn” o “solve puzzles/math problems.” 12. ‘Wag mabulag o sumugal sa mga katagang “encoding pa lang tayo,” “law of firsts,” “double your money,” “only for the risk takers” at iba pa. 13. Sa mga nag-aalok ng investment sa cryptocurrency, mag-ingat sa mga scheme na may garantiyang kikita, kailangang mag-recruit para kumita at gumagamit ng “autobot” o “automated trading system.” 14. Umiwas sa mga nag-aalok ng investment sa foreign currency na may inisyal na deposito o “margin deposit” at “maintenance margin.” Ang ganitong klaseng investment ay tinatawag na “commodity futures contract” o “leveraged foreign currency trading” at ang pag- aalok at trading nito ay kasalukuyang ipinagbabawal sa batas. Para sa ibang impormasyon, maaring bisitahin ang Investment Scam checklist sa link na ito: http://www.sec.gov.ph/public-information-2/investors- education-and-information/investment-scam-checklist/ Ang sinumang “salesmen,” “brokers,” “dealers,” o “agents” na nakikibahagi sa pag-aalok, pagbebenta at pangangalap ng pamumuhunan sa publiko ay maaaring maharap sa paglabag ng Securities Regulation Code na may penalty na aabot hanggang Php 5,000,000.00 at pagkakakulong ng 21 taon. Maging ang mga nahikayat na mamuhunan o recruit na namuhunan at nag-aalok din ng nabanggit na investment contract o securities sa publiko ay maaaring mapatawan ng kasong kriminal o kaparehas na parusang nabanggit. Muling pinapaalalahan ang publiko na HUWAG O TIGILANG MAMUHUNAN O MAKIBAHAGI sa kahit anong produkto o gawain na inaalok ng nasabing mga kaduda-dudang indibidwal o pangkat ng indibidwal at maging mapanuri sa pakikipagtransaksyon sa kanila. Kung kayo ay may nalalaman o karagdagang impormasyon sa mga nagsasagawa ng scam, maaaring makipag-ugnayan sa Enforcement and Investor Protection Department (EIPD), sa pamamagitan ng email address: epd@sec.gov.ph Page 5

body: SEC ADVISORY The Commission has received information that individuals or group of persons representing ORGANICO AGRIBUSINESS VENTURES CORPORATION (“ORGANICO”) are enticing the public to invest in the said entity online or through the internet. Based on the information communicated and gathered by the Commission, ORGANICO is engaged in soliciting investment wherein an investor must invest at least 10 shares, one (1) share costs Php1,800.00, and for every share an investor gets Php450.00 every 15 days for a total of Php2,700.00 in 3 months. Allegedly, the money invested will be used to fund the company’s diverse businesses which includes: organic farming, organic poultry, organic piggery, restaurant serving organic food, telemarketing, music studio and construction and eventually, an organic meat shop. Another investment scheme is the 90-day investment, where for every Php3,600.00 invested, one piglet is raised and sold after 3 months and the investor gets his money back with profit for a total of Php7,000.00. The public is hereby informed that ORGANICO AGRIBUSINESS VENTURES CORPORATION is NOT registered with the Commission as a corporation nor as a partnership under the Corporation Code of the Philippines and is NOT authorized to offer, solicit, sell or distribute any investment/securities. Such activities require a Secondary License from the Commission and the securities or investment product should likewise be registered with SEC before they can be offered or sold to the public under Sections 8 and 12 of the Securities Regulation Code (SRC). Consequently, those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents of ORGANICO AGRIBUSINESS VENTURES CORPORATION in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme including solicitations or recruitment through the internet may likewise be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the Securities Regulation Code and penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million pesos (P5,000,000.00) or penalty of Twenty One (21) years imprisonment or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC. Accordingly, those who invite or recruit other people to join or invest in this venture or offer contracts or securities to the public may be held liable or accordingly sanctioned or penalized in accordance with the Supreme Court decision in the case of SEC vs. Oudine Santos (G.R. No. 195542, March 19, 2014). Furthermore, the names of all those involved will be reported to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) so that the appropriate penalties and/or taxes be correspondingly assessed. In view thereof, the public is hereby advised to exercise caution before investing in these kinds of activities and to take the necessary precaution in dealing with ORGANICO AGRIBUSINESS VENTURES CORPORATION or its representatives. Should you have any information regarding the operation of the subject entity, please call the Enforcement and Investor Protection Department at telephone numbers 818-6047. For guidance of the public..
title: Organico Agribusiness Ventures Corporation

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This is to inform the public that CYFLE/CYFLE OPC is NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENTS FROM THE PUBLIC. CYFLE/CYFLE OPC through its CEO, JESTONI DARWIN EDEM is actively using Social media, particularly Facebook in promoting his company. Accordingly, interested persons may invest in his company in the following manner: 1.) Fill out the investment form; (by clicking the link as shown in the screenshot below) 2.) Wait for the Management team to contact you; 3.) check and finalize the details of your investment; 4.) Follow the terms and get your initial investment; and 5.) A contract with a corresponding address will be handed to you. The minimum investment is Php. 50,000.00 for a one (1) year term with up to 30% return of investment. Briefly, an “investment contract” exists when there is an investment or placement of money in a common enterprise with a reasonable expectation of profits to be derived from the efforts of others which is prominent in the scheme of CYFLE/CYFLE OPC. As such, the Securities Regulation Code (SRC) requires that said offer and/or sale of securities must be duly registered with the Commission and that the concerned entity and/or its agents should have the appropriate registration and/or license to sell such securities to the public. Based on the Commission’s database, CYFLE/CYFLE OPC is REGISTERED with the Commission. However, it OPERATES WITHOUT THE NECESSARY LICENSE AND/OR AUTHORITY to solicit, accept or take investments/placements from the public nor to issue investment contracts and other forms of securities defined under Section 3 of the Securities Regulation Code (SRC). The scheme employed by, CYFLE/CYFLE OPC has the characteristics of a “Ponzi Scheme” where money from new investors are used in paying “fake profits” to prior investors and is designed mainly to favor its top recruiters and prior risk takers and is detrimental to subsequent members in case of scarcity of new investors. The offering and selling of securities in the form of investment contracts using the “Ponzi Scheme” which is fraudulent and unsustainable, is NOT a registrable security. The Commission will not issue a License to Sell Securities to the Public to persons or entities that are engaged in this business or scheme. Moreover, the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act prohibits the commission of “Investment fraud”, defined as any form of deceptive solicitation of investments from the public which includes Ponzi schemes and such other schemes involving the promise or offer of profits or returns sourced from the investments or contributions made by the investors themselves and the offering or selling of investment schemes to the public without a license or permit from the SEC. In view thereof, the public is hereby advised NOT TO INVEST or to STOP INVESTING in the investment scheme being offered by CYFLE/CYFLE OPC as well as to any other entities having the same or similar schemes and to exercise caution in dealing with any individuals or group of persons soliciting investments or recruiting investors for and on behalf of CYFLE/CYFLE OPC. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents, representatives, promoters, uplines, recruiters, influencers, endorsers and enablers of CYFLE/CYFLE OPC, in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered by the said entity including soliciting investments or recruiting investors through the internet may be held criminally liable under Section 11 of the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) and under Section 28 of the SRC which are both penalized separately with a maximum fine of Five Million Pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or imprisonment of Twenty One (21) years or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC (SEC vs. Oudine Santos, G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). Furthermore, the names of all those involved will be reported to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) so that the appropriate penalties and/or taxes be correspondingly assessed. Should you have any information regarding any investment solicitation by any individual or group of individuals on behalf of CYFLE/CYFLE OPC, please send your report through email at epd@sec.gov.ph. For the information and guidance of the public. Makati City, 17 July 2024

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This is to inform the public that CENTUROS FINANCE GROUP II is NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENTS FROM THE PUBLIC. This Advisory is prompted by the information gathered by the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) that individuals or group of persons representing the above-named entity headed by its CEO, OLIVER PASCUA are soliciting investments from the public purportedly to be invested in cryptocurrency trading. Based on the Commission’s database, the said entity is not registered with the Commission as a corporation, OPC or a partnership. The entity likewise has not been issued by the Commission any license or permit to sell or offer securities to the public or to conduct any activities regulated by the Commission. CENTUROS entices the public to invest online or through the internet in three (3) programs, the Alpha, Bravo and Charlie. GUARANTEED PROFIT PROGRAMS INVESTMENT PERIOD RATE AMOUNT (PHP) (Php) ALPHA 1,000 to10,000 6 days 80% 1,800 to 18,000 BRAVO 2,000 to 20,000 8 days 120% 4,400 to 44,000 CHARLIE 5,000 to 50,000 10 days 160% 13,000 to 130,000 The said entity likewise offers a Referral Bonus equivalent to 5% of the investment received by the entity from the referals made by its members. Based on the entity’s representation, the purported source of the guaranteed income offered by the entity to the public comes from its cryptocurrency trading activities allegedly using Binance as its platform. The investment offering by CENTUROS contitutes selling or offering for sale of unregistered securities in the form of investment contract as the investors are enticed to earn guaranteed profit ranging from 80% to 160% by simply investing their money to CENTUROS in violation of Sections 8, 26 and 28 of the Securities Regulation Code. By the mere fact of CENTUROS’ absence of primary registration with this Commission either as a corporation, one-person corporation or as a partnership, it follows that it cannot be issued secondary license to solicit, offer, and sell investment to the public as required under Section 8 of the SRC. Hence, the offering of the subject entity of unregistered securities to the public constitutes violations of Sections 8, 26 and 28 of the SRC. The same likewise constitutes a violation of Section 11 of the Republic Act No. 11765 also known as the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act as the offering and selling of unregistered securities is defined as investment fraud under Section 3(f) of the same act. Accordingly, the Commission warns all unscrupulous individuals and/or entities that strict penalties are imposed for violations of the Securities Regulation Code, the Revised Corporation Code of the Philippines and such other laws, rules and regulations enforced by the Commission. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents of CENTUROS FINANCE GROUP II vis-à-vis OLIVER PASCUA in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered by said entity including solicitations and recruitment through the internet may be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the SRC and Section 11 of the FCPA and separately penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or penalty of Twenty-one (21) years of imprisonment or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC (G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). In view thereof, the public is advised NOT TO INVEST or STOP INVESTING in any investment scheme being offered by CENTUROS FINANCE GROUP II vis-à-vis OLIVER PASCUA as well as in any other entities having the same or similar schemes and to exercise caution in dealing with any individuals or group of persons soliciting investments or recruiting investors for and on behalf of CENTUROS FINANCE GROUP II vis-à-vis OLIVER PASCUA. Should you have any information regarding any investment solicitation by any individuals or group of individuals on behalf of CENTUROS FINANCE GROUP II vis-à-vis OLIVER PASCUA, please send your report to the ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT at epd@sec.gov.ph. For the guidance of the public. Makati City, 19 September 2023.

body: ENFORCEMENT & INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This ADVISORY is prompted by inquiries and complaints with regard to the solicitation activities of one DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR. Based on the information gathered, Ms. DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR appears to be engaged in investment-taking activities not authorized by the Commission. Reportedly, DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR is engaged in clothing business under DTI registered business name, Danea Clothing Wholesaling, and other trade names such as Mane Overruns, Must Have Online Shop, Mane Investments, and Mane Emergency Loans. She lured the victims with great return of investment evidenced by written investment contracts. Specifically, under the Normal Exclusive Investment Scheme, an initial investment of Php25,000.00 guarantees a total return of Php30,000.00 (20%); Php100,000.00 promised a total return of Php150,000.00 (50%) with a lock in period of one month and expected weekly return of investment. Moreover, a Normal Initial Investment of Php25,000.00 guarantees Php27,500.00 (10%); Php100,000.00 to Php125,000.00 (25%) return of investment in one week. Furthermore, there is an additional commission fee ranging from Php500.00 to Php5,000.00 for required Referrals. Likewise, DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR offered double the amount of investment or 100% interest either in a month or a week for Exclusive VIP Member who has Php1,000,000.00 to Php2,000,000.00 or more. Based on the Commission’s database, the name DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR is NOT registered with the Commission either as a corporation or as a partnership. Further, DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR it is NOT AUTHORIZED to solicit investments/placements from the public nor to issue investment contracts and other forms of securities since she has not secured prior registration and/or license from the Commission as prescribed under Sections 8 and 28 of the Securities Regulation Code. The public is hereby advised NOT TO INVEST or STOP INVESTING in any investment scheme being offered by DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR or any individual or group of persons allegedly for or on behalf of DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR and to exercise caution in dealing with any individuals or group of persons soliciting investments for and on her behalf. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents of DANEA RUBY CARDONES SOLMAYOR in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered by her including solicitations and recruitment through the internet may likewise be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the SRC and penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million pesos (P5,000,000.00) or penalty of Twenty-one (21) years of imprisonment or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC. Also, those who invite or recruit others to join or invest in such venture or offer investment contracts or securities to the public may incur criminally liability, or otherwise be sanctioned or penalized accordingly as held by the Supreme Court in the case of Securities and Exchange Commission vs. Oudine Santos (G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). Furthermore, the names of all those involved will be reported to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) so that the appropriate penalties and/or taxes be correspondingly assessed. This Department is taking appropriate action against unauthorized investment taking activities and investment scams. Hence, if you have been approached to join and invest in an entity which does not have the proper authority to solicit investments/placements from the public, we encourage you to cooperate with us immediately report these activities to the ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT through email at epd@sec.gov.ph For the guidance of the public. Pasay City, 26 October 2021.

body: A D V I S O R Y “ R2R AGRI INDUSTRY CO. and/or R2R FINANCE” This is to inform the public that R2R AGRI INDUSTRY CO./R2R FINANCE is NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENTS FROM THE PUBLIC. This ADVISORY is prompted by reports and information gathered by the Commission that individuals or groups of persons headed by RENZ REYTON FRANCO are enticing the public, through social media platforms, to invest in R2R AGRI INDUSTRY CO./R2R FINANCE. Based on information gathered by the Commission, RENZ REYTON FRANCO introduced himself as the alleged “Hedge Fund Manager” of R2R Finance and represented that he has experience as an agripreneur, e-commerce manager, and Forex/Crypto trader. He claimed that through his years of experience in business and financial trading, he developed a system intended to generate profits through various business ventures and financial activities. Further, he represented that R2R Finance allegedly operates through three (3) pillars, namely: 1. Agri-Business through R2R Agribrew and its purported coffee farm business, which allegedly serves as a “real asset” and source of stable income; 2. E-Commerce through a drop shipping business model; and 3. Forex and Crypto Trading utilizing purported “hedge fund strategies” intended to generate significant returns. As posted online, R2R AGRI INDUSTRY CO./R2R FINANCE is offering investments opportunities to the public, as shown below: Page 2 of 3 The public is hereby informed that an “investment contract” exists when there is an investment or placement of money in a common enterprise with a reasonable expectation of profits to be derived from the efforts of others. Such characteristics appear to be present in the scheme employed by R2R AGRI INDUSTRY CO./R2R FINANCE. As such, the Securities Regulation Code (SRC) requires that the offer and sale of securities be duly registered with the Commission and that the concerned entity and/or its agents possess the necessary registration and/or license to offer and sell such securities to the public. Records of the Commission show that R2R AGRI INDUSTRY CO. is registered with the Commission as a corporation. However, it is NOT AUTHORIZED to solicit investments from the public considering that it has not secured the requisite registration and/or license from the Commission as prescribed under Sections 8 and 28 of the Securities Regulation Code. Such schemes are designed primarily to benefit top recruiters and early participants and become unsustainable and detrimental to later investors once recruitment of new investors declines. The offering and selling of securities in the form of investment contracts through a Ponzi Scheme is fraudulent and unsustainable and the Commission will never issue a License to Sell Securities to the Public to persons or entities engaged in such business or schemes. body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This is to inform the public that GERCEL APPAREL SHOP is NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENTS FROM THE PUBLIC. This ADVISORY is prompted by reports and information gathered by the Commission that a certain person representing an entity named GERCEL APPAREL SHOP is enticing the public to invest their money in the said entity with a promise of high monetary rewards or profits. Based on the reports and information gathered, GERCEL APPAREL SHOP is an online store enticing the public by offering investments. They will give the 20% interest weekly to the capitalist, while they earn 50%-100% on daily live selling. Interested capitalist will fill-up a form, then they will share the DTI permit, provide a contract and copy of their ID. The income will be sent weekly through GCASH or bank deposit. Based on the Commission’s database, GERCEL APPAREL SHOP, is NOT REGISTERED as a corporation, partnership or One Person Corporation. Consequently, GERCEL APPAREL SHOP is NOT AUTHORIZED to offer, solicit, sell or distribute any investment/securities to the public. Such activities require a Secondary License from the Commission and the securities or investment product should likewise be registered with the SEC before they can be offered or sold to the public under Sections 8 and 12 of the Securities Regulation Code (SRC). Moreover, R.A. No. 11765 or the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) prohibits the commission of “Investment fraud”, defined as any form of deceptive solicitation of investments from the public which includes Ponzi schemes and such other schemes involving the promise or offer of profits or returns sourced from the investments or contributions made by the investors themselves and the offering or selling of investment schemes to the public without a license or permit from the SEC. In view thereof, the public is hereby advised NOT TO INVEST or to STOP INVESTING in the investment scheme being offered by GERCEL APPAREL SHOP. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents, representatives, promoters, uplines, recruiters, influencers, endorsers and enablers of GERCEL APPAREL SHOP, in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered by the said entity including soliciting investments or recruiting investors through the internet may be held criminally liable under Section 11 of the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) and Section 28 of the SRC which are penalized separately with a maximum fine of Five Million Pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or imprisonment of Twenty One (21) years or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC. (SEC vs. Oudine Santos, G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This is to inform the public that S&M VENTURES is NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENT FROM THE PUBLIC. Based on the reports and information gathered by the Commission, S&M VENTURES is engaged in property rental unit particularly at Azure Urban Resort Residences located at Km. 16 West Service Road, Brgy. Marcelo Green, Bicutan, Paranaque City. Its owner/ promoter, PAMELA SHAYNE R. GOZO is actively enticing (through S&M VENTURES’ Facebook page) the public to be their business partner. As posted online, S&M VENTURES, is offering to the public to invest in its projects, namely: a.) renovation and construction of additional units at Azure Urban Resort Residences; and 2.) investment in the rental units at Azure Urban Resort Residences. Accordingly, the minimum investment is from Php20,000.00 to Php300,000.00. Thereafter, the investor earns a passive income every month. S&M VENTURES claims that the investor has nothing to do except sit back and unwind while they handle the guest bookings, seamless check-ins and check-outs as well as the promotional aspects of renting on Airbnb. In this regard, the public is made aware that an “investment contract,” a kind of security, exists when there is an investment or placement of money in a common enterprise with a reasonable expectation of profits to be derived from the efforts of others which is prominent in the scheme of, S&M VENTURES. As such, the Securities Regulation Code (SRC) requires that said offer and/or sale of securities must be duly registered with the Commission and that the concerned entity and/or its agents should have the appropriate registration and/or license to sell such securities to the public. Based on the Commission’s database, S&M VENTURES, is NOT REGISTERED as a corporation or partnership and OPERATES WITHOUT THE NECESSARY LICENSE AND/OR AUTHORITY to solicit, accept or take investments/placements from the public nor to issue investment contracts and other forms of securities defined under Section 3 of the Securities Regulation Code (SRC). The scheme employed by, S&M VENTURES has the characteristics of a “Ponzi Scheme” where money from new investors are used in paying “fake profits” to prior investors and is designed mainly to favor its top recruiters and prior risk takers and is detrimental to subsequent members in case of scarcity of new investors. The offering and selling of securities in the form of investment contracts using the “Ponzi Scheme” which is fraudulent and unsustainable, is NOT a registrable security. The Commission will not issue a License to Sell Securities to the Public to persons or entities that are engaged in this business or scheme. Moreover, the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act prohibits the commission of “Investment fraud”, defined as any form of deceptive solicitation of investments from the public which includes Ponzi schemes and such other schemes involving the promise or offer of profits or returns sourced from the investments or contributions made by the investors themselves and the offering or selling of investment schemes to the public without a license or permit from the SEC. In view thereof, the public is hereby advised NOT TO INVEST or to STOP INVESTING in the investment scheme being offered by, S&M VENTURES as well as to any other entities having the same or similar schemes and to exercise caution in dealing with any individuals or group of persons soliciting investments or recruiting investors for and on behalf of S&M VENTURES. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents, representatives, promoters, uplines, recruiters, influencers, endorsers and enablers of S&M VENTURES, in selling or convincing people to invest in the investment scheme being offered by the said entity including soliciting investments or recruiting investors through the internet may be held criminally liable under Section 11 of the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) and under Section 28 of the SRC and both penalized separately with a maximum fine of Five Million Pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or imprisonment of Twenty One (21) years or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC (SEC vs. Oudine Santos, G.R. No. 195542, 19 March 2014). Furthermore, the names of all those involved will be reported to the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) so that the appropriate penalties and/or taxes be correspondingly assessed. Should you have any information regarding any investment solicitation by any individual or group of individuals on behalf of S&M VENTURES, please send your report through email at epd@sec.gov.ph. For the information and guidance of the public. Makati City, 05 December 2023.

body: SEC ADVISORY 20 October 2016 FOREIGN EXCHANGE TRADING The advisory is prompted by the complaints of retail investors who lost their moneys to forex trading. The public is advised that TRADING OF COMMODITIES FUTURES CONTRACTS IN THE PHILIPPINES (including Foreign Exchange Trading as consistently held by the Commission) and the pertinent RULES ARE STILL SUSPENDED pursuant to Paragraph 4 of Rule II of the Amended Rules and Regulations implementing the Securities Regulation Code. Based on the reports, huge amount of money has been invested (usually in US dollars) in forex trading corporations where investors opened margin accounts to enable them to trade in foreign currency. The so-called “experts” of the forex trading corporations execute foreign trade positions in behalf of the investors on the representation that investors shall gain profit as in the stock market. It has to be reiterated that under Section 11 of the Securities Regulation Code “no person shall offer, sell or enter into commodity futures contract except in accordance with rules and regulations and orders of the Commission may prescribe in the public interest”. The investors should also take the cue from the ruling laid down in Onapal v. Court of Appeals (G.R. No. 90707, February 3, 1993) where the Supreme Court stated in this wise: “xxx The payments made under said contract were payments of difference in prices arising out of the rise or fall in the market price above or below the contract price thus making it purely gambling and declared null and void by law.” The public is encouraged to report to the Commission entities operating Foreign Exchange Trading and those acting as agents of these operators. Our telephone numbers are: 584-6047; 584-7652 References: http://www.bsp.gov.ph/publications/media.asp?id=1604 http://www.sec.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/2016AdvisoryAshokfx.pdf http://www.sec.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/2015_SEC-Advisory_Metisetrade_Inc.pdf http://www.sec.gov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/2015_SEC_CDO_CASE_No_04-15- 016_Metistrade_Inc.pdf

body: ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT SEC ADVISORY This is to inform the public that REVEAL BEAUTY AND WELLNESS DIGITAL MARKETING OPC., doing business under the name and style of: REVEAL MARKETING/REVEAL MARKETING PH/REVEAL MARKETING TEAM PH (‘REVEAL’ for brevity) and the individuals offering investments under its name are NOT AUTHORIZED TO SOLICIT INVESTMENTS FROM THE PUBLIC. This Advisory was prompted by reports received and information gathered by the Commission that individuals or group of persons affiliated with REVEAL, led by its CEO, Willyn Morla, and VP, Lady Lyn Sinfuego, are engaged in an investment scheme called “Shareholder’s program.” As posted on its Facebook Pages1, REVEAL represents to be engaged in MLM (Multi- level Marketing) “intended to help the people to have an extra passive income through investments.” REVEAL’s investment scheme includes a “shareholder’s program” which offers different modes where the public can purchase a share and expect a corresponding profit depending on the type of share they choose. The investment opportunity being offered by REVEAL is a form of securities as the elements of investment contract are present in its investment offerings. REVEAL’s shareholder program intends to entice the public to invest in them by offering different types of shares from the Basic share, Standard share, and Premium share. 1. Basic share – 20% in 7 days with a minimum purchase of 1,000 pesos and a maximum purchase of 30,000 pesos. 2. Standard share – 50% in 15 days with a minimum purchase of 1,000 pesos and a maximum purchase of 200,000 pesos. 3. Premium share – 130% in 30 days with a minimum purchase of 1,000 pesos and a maximum purchase of 1,000,000 pesos. 1 https://www.facebook.com/ReveaIMarketing; https://www.facebook.com/gpgprospera; https://www.facebook.com/revealmktgph; https://www.facebook.com/revealmktg.glow The records of the Commission show that REVEAL BEAUTY AND WELLNESS DIGITAL MARKETING OPC was registered with the Commission as a one-person corporation on 09 May 2023. However, it is NOT AUTHORIZED to solicit investments from the public since it has not secured prior registration and/or secondary license from the Commission to engage in such activity. Further verification also found that the entities REVEAL MARKETING/REVEAL MARKETING PH/REVEAL MARKETING TEAM PH, are not registered either as a corporation, one- person corporation (OPC), or as a partnership. The investment scheme being offered by REVEAL BEAUTY AND WELLNESS DIGITAL MARKETING OPC/REVEAL MARKETING/REVEAL MARKETING PH/REVEAL MARKETING TEAM PH, seem to be fraudulent as it engaged in the offering and/or selling of unregistered securities to the public in violation of Sections 8, 26 and 28 of the Securities Regulation Code. Further, the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) specifically provides that any form of deceptive solicitation such as offering or selling of investment scheme from the public without a secondary license or permit from the Commission constitute investment fraud and is an unlawful activity in violation of Section 11 of the said Act. Accordingly, the Commission warns all unscrupulous individuals and/or entities that strict penalties are imposed for violations of the Securities Regulation Code and the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act (FCPA) and such other laws, rules and regulations enforced by the Commission. Those who act as salesmen, brokers, dealers or agents of REVEAL in selling or convincing people to invest in what appears to be an investment scheme being offered by said entity including solicitations and recruitment through the internet may be prosecuted and held criminally liable under Section 28 of the SRC and Section 11 of the FCPA and both penalized with a maximum fine of Five Million pesos (Php5,000,000.00) or penalty of Twenty-one (21) years of imprisonment or both pursuant to Section 73 of the SRC. In view thereof, the public is advised NOT TO INVEST or STOP INVESTING in any investment scheme being offered by REVEAL as well as in other entities having the same or similar schemes and to exercise caution in dealing with any individuals or group of persons soliciting investments or recruiting investors for and on behalf of REVEAL. Should you have any information regarding any investment solicitation by any individuals or group of individuals on behalf of REVEAL., please send your report to the ENFORCEMENT AND INVESTOR PROTECTION DEPARTMENT at epd@sec.gov.ph For the guidance of the public. Makati City, 08 February 2024.
